clue.text: New and sensational French art in fresh photo unexpectedly cut by this paper

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters of fresh photo come out in a surprising new order

parts.note: in French tu es means thou art, so art is ES
FT is the Financial Times, the paper printing this puzzle, whose initials cut into the mix

explanation.surface: A newspaper boasts of a racy new French artwork shown in a freshly cropped photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'cut by' set the French verb and the paper's initials among the photo words; 'unexpectedly' shuffles all fourteen letters. Art comes from French tu es, thou art.
explanation.definitionFit: News just printed is brand new and often sensational, the phrase describing freshly reported stories.

clue.text: Good old Ireland's cracking beer getting past pirate

indicators.note: cracking means breaking open the beer so other letters can go inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Erin is an old poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An old Irish beer is good enough to see off a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbary corsairs sailing from Algiers were called by this name, so it denotes a pirate of that coast.

clue.text: Incendiary material in article about bribe

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the article's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to palm someone is to bribe them, as in greasing a palm

explanation.surface: A news article about bribery concerns incendiary material.
explanation.definitionFit: Jellied petrol used in firebombs, the classic incendiary weapon substance.

clue.text: One's spotted in dance outfit following a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the central letter of the dance garment is swapped for another

parts.note: a leotard is the close-fitting garment dancers wear

explanation.surface: A dancer is noticed in their leotard after changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter T of LEOTARD becomes P. 'spotted' looks like 'noticed', but it describes the big cat's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat famously has a spotted coat, so it is one that is spotted.

clue.text: Former leader of Ireland, old twat under house arrest?

indicators.note: under house arrest means the following letters are held inside the house abbreviation
arrest means holding, so the house abbreviation contains the other letters

parts.note: to twat is slang for to strike, to hit

explanation.surface: A one-time Irish leader, an old fool, is confined to their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twat' looks like a noun insult but is the slang verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Japanese emperor from 1926 to 1989, a ruler of the past.

clue.text: Boundless karma made man fleet

indicators.note: boundless means each of the three words loses its outer letters, its bounds

explanation.surface: Unlimited karma made a man quick on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like the adjective for quick, but it is the noun for a group of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was a great fleet of warships, and the word means any naval fleet.

clue.text: Muse over having exposed unlimited food for Highlands, say?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the Muse's name is read backwards

parts.note: Clio is the Muse of history

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: exposed means naked

explanation.surface: A poet broods over food for the Scottish Highlands after being laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlands' here are Highland cattle, the shaggy Scottish breed, not the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Compressed seed residue after oil extraction is fed to livestock, such as Highland cattle.

clue.text: Break in appeal holding back Queen's Speech?

indicators.note: holding means the word for appeal contains the other letters

parts.note: IT means sex appeal, as in the it girl

indicators.note: back means the queen's sound is read in reverse

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, whose speech is a purr

explanation.surface: A monarch's address is interrupted by an appeal being withheld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's Speech' is not the royal address in Parliament; a queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst or force one's way into a place suddenly is to break in.

clue.text: When an upward trend in battery production is likely to occur?

definitions.text: When an upward trend in battery production is likely to occur?

parts.words: When an upward trend in battery production is likely to occur?
parts.note: battery is read as what is made of batter, and the upward trend is tossing it into the air on Shrove Tuesday

explanation.surface: An economist asks when output of batteries might rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, when people make batter treats and toss them high in the pan, is the day meant.

clue.text: Waited to the very end, closing a wine shop

parts.note: bode is an old past tense of bide, to wait

indicators.note: to the very end picks only the final letter of the word closing

explanation.surface: Someone waited until closing time at a wine shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish term for a cellar or shop selling wine, used for such shops in English.

clue.text: A pimento hybrid that's potentially toxic

indicators.note: hybrid means a cross, so the letters of a pimento are mixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cross-bred pepper might be poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: These are compounds formed in rotting protein, once blamed for food poisoning, so a substance that may poison.

clue.text: I confirm if farmer needs a bit of a change

indicators.text: needs a bit of a change
indicators.note: a change means the letters of if farmer get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that a farmer could use a slight change.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who says I confirm is one who asserts or declares something to be true.

clue.text: Profit reported in tax-free scheme — excellent returns by end of month

parts.note: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account, a tax-free savings scheme

indicators.note: returns means the term for excellent is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of month

explanation.surface: Gains declared in a tax-free savings plan show excellent returns at month-end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profit reported' is the definition by sound: a prophet, spoken aloud, sounds like profit. ISA is a UK tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the major Old Testament prophets, and prophet sounds like profit.

clue.text: Revolutionary modest backing brings comfort

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: backing means the word for modest is read backwards

parts.note: pure, as in chaste, is a sense of modest

explanation.surface: Supporting a humble revolutionary brings solace.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to raise their spirits, the phrasal verb meaning make happier.

clue.text: Unopened room in shadow offering protection

indicators.note: in places the trimmed room inside the shadow word

parts.note: umbra is the dark central part of a shadow

indicators.note: unopened means the room word loses its first letter

parts.note: a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A dark room with the door shut gives shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in an umbrella body, it means covering or sheltering many.

clue.text: Unknown bishop blocking organ stops thugs

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: blocking means the bishop's letter sits inside the organ stops

parts.note: oboe is the name of a reed stop on an organ
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An unidentified bishop obstructing the organ halts some louts.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobs are loutish hooligans, the British slang for aggressive young men.

clue.text: Reduction once meant bet should be dissolved

indicators.note: dissolved means broken up, so the letters of meant bet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager once intended should now be cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word for abatement meant a lessening or reduction.

clue.text: This month, see Andy regularly appearing as a substitute

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of see Andy, starting with the second

explanation.surface: This month Andy will be seen standing in as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in place of something else, acting as a replacement.

clue.text: Place order on Amazon's first book? Cool

indicators.note: on means placed next to the earlier letters
first takes the opening letter of the word Amazon's

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A shopper orders their first book online, calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance and composure under pressure is exactly what being cool means as a noun.

clue.text: Put away after first solitary

indicators.note: after means this piece comes after the first piece

parts.note: one is first, number one
to off someone is slang for killing them, putting them away

explanation.surface: Something is stored away after the first single item.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique that happens only once is single, unrepeated and alone of its kind.

clue.text: Energy-free gluten crackers — strange Bhutanese bread?

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the remaining letters are jumbled
free means without, so the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
rum is old slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Gluten-free crackers make for some odd bread from Bhutan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, not food, despite the gluten and crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the currency of Bhutan, and bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Country in which solvers look to get caught

indicators.note: caught means heard, as when catching what someone said

parts.note: solvers are addressed as you, and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: A puzzle in which solvers seek to be trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, you gander sounds like the African country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a landlocked nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Stiff cloth about to be coated with glue

indicators.note: coated with means wrapped in, so the glue word surrounds the short word for about

parts.note: cement is a glue or adhesive
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A rigid fabric gets coated in glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like rigid, but a stiff is slang for a corpse: this is a waxed burial wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxed wrapping laid over a dead body, so the cloth for a corpse.

clue.text: Very nearly skinned fish — good man

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters of the fish are stripped off

parts.note: salmon is a fish
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A good man nearly skinned a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means nearly but not quite, so very nearly works as a synonym.

clue.text: Competent spouse fully gives more than needed

indicators.note: the two words supply more letters than required, the needed ones sitting within them

explanation.surface: A capable husband or wife gives over and above the call of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and serviceable, of practical help: a sense close to able.

clue.text: Supplements potential online publicity blocker as discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: something that might stop an advert online would be an ad ender

explanation.surface: Extra pages could serve as an ad blocker, as mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a non-rhotic British accent, ad ender sounds like the plural of addendum.
explanation.definitionFit: Additions appended to a book or document are extra supplementary material.
